title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: The roadmap details and existing bot controls are supported. The rollout checklist nevertheless tells administrators to pilot the new list through targeted meeting policies, although Microsoft has not documented whether those policies configure or assign the list.

claims.claim: The feature belongs to Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an administrator-configured list of external meeting bots allowed to join meetings hosted in the organisation.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure a list of external meeting bots which are allowed to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Existing Teams bot detection uses signals collected during meeting join.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.claim: With detection enabled, detected bots are placed in the lobby irrespective of meeting lobby configuration.
claims.quote: The participants detected as bots are placed in the meeting lobby irrespective of the lobby configuration for the meeting.

claims.claim: Detected bots require explicit admission under the existing approval setting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide allows presenters to admit detected bots depending on the meeting setting.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: The Bot Identification Program page instead describes detected bots as requiring organiser approval.
claims.quote: Even when a meeting allows participants to bypass the lobby, detected bots still require organizer approval before joining.

claims.claim: The existing bot setting defaults to When detected, require approval before joining (RequireApprovalWhenDetected).
claims.quote: When detected, require approval before joining | RequireApprovalWhenDetected | (default) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The external-bots guide lists detection with approval and Do not detect bots as its existing options.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | AllowBots | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference additionally documents BlockDetectedBots to block detected external bots.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.

claims.claim: External notetaker bots may record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.
claims.quote: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.claim: External bots may store meeting data in third-party systems outside organisational compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: Some external bots may not be detected.
claims.quote: Some external bots may not be detected.

claims.claim: The Teams Bot Identification Program is a public preview for software vendors building meeting bot experiences.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Teams Bot Identification Program (Public Preview)
Microsoft is also introducing the Teams Bot Identification Program to support independent software vendors (ISVs) that build meeting bot experiences for Teams.

claims.claim: Eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft through the program.
claims.quote: Through this program, eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft and include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests.

claims.claim: The program lets eligible providers include a self-identification marker in meeting join requests.
claims.quote: Through this program, eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft and include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not state how the Bot Identification Program relates to the planned allowed list.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external bots list identity Bot Identification Program; Microsoft Teams external bots allowed list how bot identified high friction lobby. Read teams-bot-identification and manage-external-bots; no list relationship stated.

claims.claim: Bot detection may occasionally misclassify human participants.
claims.quote: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.

claims.claim: Misclassified participants can be admitted from the lobby.
claims.quote: you can rectify the situation by admitting the participants from the lobby and marking them with "This is not a bot" option.

claims.claim: The This is not a bot option corrects the representation of misclassified participants.
claims.quote: marking them with "This is not a bot" option. This action changes the representation as a standard human participant in that specific meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether blocked participants can use the lobby correction route or have a block overridden.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams BlockDetectedBots blocked human participant override admit This is not a bot allowed bots list. Read manage-external-bots and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; lobby correction is documented, but overriding a block is not.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide lists no licence or meter for the existing setting.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence or meter.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure more granular and advanced controls for managing external bots and their access to meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: The existing external-bots setting is assigned through meeting policies at user or group level.
claims.quote: Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: The existing setting can be configured tenant-wide using the default org-wide meeting policy.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy

claims.claim: The existing setting can be configured for specific users or groups through targeted meeting policies.
claims.quote: or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: The external-bots guide applies to meetings and not events.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: [checkmark for yes] Meetings [x for no] Events

claims.claim: The external-bots page does not name the admin role required to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched: admin role required to edit meeting policies within the fully read manage-external-bots page. It says admins configure the policy, but gives no role name; the claim is limited to that page.

claims.claim: Learn recommends allowing only organisers and co-organisers to admit lobby participants.
claims.quote: Configure the meetings hosted in your organization to only allow Organizers and co-organizers to admit participants from the meeting lobby.

claims.claim: The lobby admission setting is in the Meeting join & lobby section of a meeting policy.
claims.quote: In the Meeting join & lobby sections, update the settings that you want to change: ... Who can admit from lobby

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the existing external-bots setting as approving named bots.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed list external meeting notetaker bots allowlist admin setting PowerShell Graph ExternalBotAccessMode 580451. Read manage-external-bots and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; existing options manage detection, approval or blocking, not named approval.

claims.claim: The existing bot setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: This setting is present in the Meeting Join and Lobby section of Meeting policies. Look for "Manage external bots and their access to meetings" and select the appropriate option.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected configures bot detection with lobby approval.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The planned allowed-bots list can be piloted with a targeted meeting policy and assigned to users or groups before changing the default org-wide policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams external bot allowlist default policy assignment scope. Read roadmap, manage-external-bots and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; targeted/default policy configuration is documented for existing bot handling, not the new list.
claims.fix: Replace 'Pilot with a targeted meeting policy for a small group before changing the default org-wide policy.' with 'Confirm the list's documented configuration and assignment scope before deciding how to pilot it.' Remove 'assigning a policy to the right users or groups' from the Cost and licensing list of work for the planned list.

claims.claim: Learn asks administrators to report undetected external meeting bots through the Feedback option in Teams.
claims.quote: Help improve the system by reporting any undetected external meeting bots to us via the Feeback option in Teams.
